title: chapters/NN.json — one chapter and its claims

text.description: Plain prose. No headings, bullets or footnote markers.

passages.description: Declared point-of-view passages (history/domains/pivotal-history/voice.md §2). Allowed only in a project whose domain has a point-of-view ladder; a History Writer story has none.

mode.description: L1, immersive frame. L0 is everything not declared; L2 (fiction) is not a mode here.

from.description: The passage's first words, copied exactly from `text`.

to.description: Its last words, copied exactly, after `from`.

text.description: The assertion as written in the chapter.

anchor.description: A few words, copied exactly, of the ONE sentence in the prose this claim supports. tools/cite.py places the reader's note after that sentence; the gate fails an anchor found in no sentence or in several.

evidence.description: A VERBATIM contiguous quote from that source's fetched text, at least thresholds.minQuoteWords words. Copy it exactly.

kind.description: era: context about the time and place (capped). quote: words the chapter puts in quotation marks. cast: who a person or a people was, at the first meeting (a pivotal-history story; `about` names the cast entry). scale: the figure a modern comparison needs (Manhattan's length), sourced like any fact; a sentence whose every claim is a scale claim is relaxed as a writer's sentence is (history/domains/pivotal-history/voice.md §2a).

about.description: For a `cast` claim: the dossier people[] or peoples[] `name` it introduces.
